title: Stochastic Models Underlying Croston’s Method for Intermittent Demand Forecasting
supported_claim: Croston smooths positive amounts and inter-arrival times; conventional point forecasts do not inherently define a coherent intermittent predictive distribution.
limitations: Analyses proposed stochastic underpinnings; does not prove that Croston point forecasts are universally inferior or validate enterprise spending.
license_status: Copyright 2005 John Wiley & Sons shown in PDF; no open reuse license verified.

title: The accuracy of intermittent demand estimates
authors_or_org: Aris A. Syntetos; John E. Boylan
supported_claim: Original comparison of SMA, SES, Croston and authors’ new method on 3,000 automotive intermittent series; supports SBA as an empirical benchmark.
limitations: Full paper not retrieved; formula verified independently in original ADIDA research paper S04. Inventory dataset transfer is unvalidated.
license_status: Unverified; institutional availability is not a license.

title: Intermittent demand: Linking forecasting to inventory obsolescence
authors_or_org: Ruud H. Teunter; Aris A. Syntetos; M. Zied Babai
kind: primary research, institutional version of record
supported_claim: TSB updates occurrence probability every period and amount on positive demand; addresses Croston/SBA zero-run nondecay and obsolescence in studied simulations.
limitations: Unbiasedness and comparative performance are under paper conditions; true zero observations are assumed. Does not identify pauses or missing feeds.
license_status: Elsevier all rights reserved; repository describes personal-use/Taverne restrictions, not a general reuse license.

title: An Aggregate–Disaggregate Intermittent Demand Approach (ADIDA) to Forecasting: An Empirical Proposition and Analysis
authors_or_org: Konstantinos Nikolopoulos; Aris A. Syntetos; John E. Boylan; Fotios Petropoulos; Vassilios Assimakopoulos
published_or_version: 2011 JORS 62(3):544–554; repository labels document early preprint; DOI 10.1057/jors.2010.32
supported_claim: Aggregation reduces intermittency while losing timing; original study evaluates 5,000 RAF series; gives SBA correction using interval smoothing coefficient.
limitations: Preprint may differ from version of record; inventory lead-time target does not establish calendar-budget performance.
license_status: Repository states copyright/moral rights retained; no broad reuse license verified.

title: Forecast Combinations for Intermittent Demand
published_or_version: Author preprint dated 2014-05-24; published JORS 66(6):914–924, 2015; DOI 10.1057/jors.2014.62
supported_claim: Compares method and temporal combinations; multiple temporal aggregation can reduce need to select one aggregation level; excessive aggregation and data length matter.
limitations: RAF inventory evidence; some combinations do not improve forecasts. IMAPA implementation nomenclature verified in S06 rather than assumed identical to every paper variant.
license_status: Unverified; author-hosted access does not establish reuse permission.

title: StatsForecast Models API Reference
published_or_version: Live unversioned documentation observed 2026-10-24; exact installed/package version not established
supported_claim: Lists ADIDA, CrostonClassic, CrostonOptimized, CrostonSBA, IMAPA and TSB as sparse/intermittent models.
limitations: API availability is not validation or a pinned implementation; probabilistic support must be inspected for the exact chosen model and version.
license_status: Documentation and code licenses not inspected; unverified.

title: Stan User’s Guide: Finite Mixtures
supported_claim: Distinguishes zero-inflated count mixtures from hurdle models, including count-generated zeros and zero-truncated positive component.
limitations: An implementation guide, not enterprise-spend evidence. Statistical mixture components cannot alone establish real-world inactive states.

title: Stan Functions Reference: Unbounded Discrete Distributions
supported_claim: Poisson mean-variance equality and NB2 variance mu + mu²/phi.
limitations: Distribution identities do not establish count-process suitability, independence or time dependence.

title: Fitting Tweedie’s Compound Poisson Model to Insurance Claims Data: Dispersion Modelling
supported_claim: Poisson frequency and gamma amount imply Tweedie aggregate cost with 1<p<2; mean-power variance and dispersion modeling; possible aggregate-only estimation.
limitations: Insurance application and particular distribution assumptions; cannot accommodate negative refunds without a separate process and cannot certify arbitrary heavy tails.
license_status: Unverified; author-hosted manuscript does not grant a general reuse license.

title: Generalized linear models for dependent frequency and severity of insurance claims
authors_or_org: José Garrido; Christian Genest; Juliana Schulz
supported_claim: Conditional-severity GLM uses claim count as predictor to relax independent frequency/severity assumption; aggregate mean and variance can change.
limitations: Publisher search content retrieved; direct DOI opening returned 403. Findings are actuarial, not evidence of AI task dependence.
license_status: Publisher indexed content says open access under Creative Commons, but exact CC variant not verified; do not assume unrestricted reuse.

title: Intermittent Demand Forecasting with Renewal Processes
authors_or_org: Ali Caner Turkmen; Tim Januschowski; Yuyang Wang; Ali Taylan Cemgil
supported_claim: Renewal-process framework handles aging, clustering and quasi-periodicity and can extend to continuous-time arrivals.
limitations: Standard intermittent-demand benchmarks do not validate enterprise AI costs; availability of granular timestamps does not guarantee identifiable process parameters.
license_status: arXiv non-exclusive distribution license verified via linked license; not a blanket open-content reuse license.

title: Stan User’s Guide: Survival Models
supported_claim: Right-censored event durations contribute survival probabilities; censoring is distinct from observed completion.
limitations: Duration censoring alone does not model task-cost accumulation or informative stop rules.

title: Counting Your Customers the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model
authors_or_org: Peter S. Fader; Bruce G. S. Hardie; Ka Lok Lee
kind: primary research, author-hosted version of record
supported_claim: Joint repeat-activity and latent-dropout models; BG/NBD assumes Poisson activity while active and dropout after transactions.
limitations: Customer retention setting with absorbing inactivity; pausing/reactivation and organizational evidence can invalidate transfer to projects or staff.
license_status: Copyright 2005 INFORMS shown; no broad reuse license verified.

title: Power-law distributions in empirical data
authors_or_org: Aaron Clauset; Cosma Rohilla Shalizi; M. E. J. Newman
kind: primary research preprint with journal reference
supported_claim: Tail classification requires more than visual log-log fits; maximum likelihood, goodness-of-fit and comparison with alternative distributions.
limitations: No AI-spend dataset; generic tail methodology cannot establish enough extreme-event data for calibrated high quantiles.
license_status: arXiv non-exclusive distribution license verified via linked license; not a blanket open-content reuse license.
